study_description: The Polish Breast Cancer Study (PBCS) is a molecular epidemiology study conducted in two major cities in Poland (Warsaw and Lodz) that enrolled approximately 2,400 breast cancer cases and 2,500 controls. This large population-based study collected biological specimens to allow for the study of a wide range of biomarkers. Subject enrollment started June 1, 2000. The last day of diagnosis for eligible breast cancer cases was December 31, 2003.The final response rates to the interview for the breast cancer component of the study were 79% for breast cancer cases and 69% for controls. Among women who agreed to the interview, most of them agreed to provide biological specimens (84% of breast cancer cases and 92% of controls agreed to provide a blood sample; 82% of cases and 89% of controls agreed to provide a urine sample), and anthropometric measurements (95% of breast cancer cases and 93% controls).
